explanation: Mixing Plaster of Paris with water converts it back into gypsum, hardening into a solid mass as it does — exactly why Plaster of Paris is useful for setting fractured bones and must be stored away from moisture.

beaker_view.initial_appearance: White Plaster of Paris powder, mixed with water into a wet paste.
beaker_view.final_appearance: Set hard into solid white gypsum.
beaker_view.observation: Mixed with water, the white powder thickens and sets hard within minutes — a change in texture more than colour.
